# Desktop mode picker, remote mode and app menu

## What to build

Add the first-run **mode picker**, **remote mode** and the **app menu** to the desktop app `apps/graph-manager-desktop` (KAN-86, spec `docs/prd/desktop-app.md`).

- With no saved `mode`, the app shows `picker.html` with two choices: **Run on this computer**, which is the existing local mode, and **Connect to a server**, which takes a URL.
- Remote mode loads the remote graph-manager server's own UI in a `persist:remote` session. The user logs in on that server's normal login page, as in a browser. There are no tokens and no changes to the server.
- An unreachable server gives an error page with **Retry** and **Change server**, plus **Run on this computer** when the server is on this machine (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `[::1]`). That's what the user sees when the terminal graph-manager they connected to (through **Connect to it**) stops.
- The menu switches modes, changes the URL, opens the server log or the workspaces folder, and has Reload and DevTools.

## What already exists (from earlier tasks)

- `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/main.ts` runs local mode:
  - `startLocalServer(...)` and `loginCookie(origin, password)` from `src/localServer.ts`, then the cookie is set in `session.fromPartition("persist:local")`
  - the main window loads `origin + "/"`
  - `setWindowOpenHandler` / `will-navigate` use `classifyLink(url, origin, kind)` from `src/links.ts`
  - `dist/pages/error.html?title=&detail=&actions=` with buttons wired through `window.gmDesktop.action(name)`. The preload `src/preload.cts` exposes `gmDesktop.action`, which calls `ipcRenderer.invoke("gm:action", name)`.
  - `ipcMain.handle("gm:action")` handles `retry`, `restart`, `log` and `connect`. `error.html` renders only the buttons named in `actions`: `retry` **Retry**, `restart` **Restart server**, `log` **Open log**, `change` **Change server**, `connect` **Connect to it**, `local` **Run on this computer**.
  - When another graph-manager already runs on the data folder, local mode shows "graph-manager is already running on this computer (port N). Stop it, or connect to it." with `actions=connect,retry`. Today `connect` saves `mode: "remote"`, `remoteUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:N"` and loads that URL in a minimal `persist:remote` window. This task routes `connect` through the full remote mode below instead.
  - `localDataDir(env, home)`, `localWorkspacesDir(env, home)` in `src/localServer.ts`: `GM_DATA_DIR`/`GM_WORKSPACES_DIR` from the app's env, else `~/.graph-manager` / `~/graph-manager-workspaces`.
  - the server stops on `before-quit`
  - single-instance lock
- `src/settings.ts`: `readSettings` and `writeSettings`, with `DesktopSettings { mode?: "local" | "remote"; remoteUrl?: string; bounds? }`.

Read `src/main.ts`, `src/preload.cts`, `src/pages/error.html`, `src/settings.ts` and `src/links.ts` fully before changing anything.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/auth.ts`, the last 3 lines of `authRoutes`: `GET /api/auth/info` is public and returns `{ host: os.hostname() }`. Remote mode uses it to check that a URL is a graph-manager server.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Login.tsx`: the server's own login page that remote mode shows. It isn't changed.

## Patterns to follow

- Pure logic goes in small exported functions with unit tests (as in `src/links.ts` / `links.test.ts`). Electron calls stay in `main.ts`.
- Pages are plain HTML with inline CSS and script: system fonts, light and dark through `prefers-color-scheme`, no external resources. Match the look of `src/pages/error.html`.
- A window with the preload only ever shows `file:` pages from `dist/pages/`. A window showing a server never has the preload.

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/remote.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  ```typescript
  export type UrlCheck = { ok: true; origin: string; insecure: boolean } | { ok: false; error: string };
  /** Parses a typed server URL into its origin; `insecure` for plain http to a host other than localhost/127.0.0.1/::1. */
  export function normalizeServerUrl(input: string): UrlCheck
  /** Whether the origin's host is this machine: 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1]. */
  export function isLoopback(origin: string): boolean
  /** Whether `<origin>/api/auth/info` answers 200 with JSON `{ host: string }` within the timeout. */
  export async function probeServer(origin: string, fetchImpl = fetch, timeoutMs = 10000): Promise<{ ok: true; host: string } | { ok: false; error: string }>
  ```
  - `normalizeServerUrl`:
    - Trim the input. If it has no scheme (no `://`), prepend `https://`.
    - Only `http:` and `https:` are allowed. Otherwise return `{ ok: false, error: "Use an http:// or https:// address." }`. Unparseable input returns `{ ok: false, error: "That isn't a valid address." }`.
    - Return `new URL(x).origin`. The path, query and trailing slash are dropped.
  - `probeServer`:
    - Use `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)`.
    - Any failure → `{ ok: false, error: "No graph-manager server answered at <origin>." }`. That covers network errors, non-200, non-JSON, and `host` that isn't a string.
- **TEST** `remote.test.ts`:
  - `"gm.example.com"` → `https://gm.example.com`, `insecure: false`
  - `"http://10.0.0.5:7420/x/"` → origin `http://10.0.0.5:7420`, `insecure: true`
  - `"http://localhost:7420"` → `insecure: false`
  - `"ftp://x"` → the error
  - `isLoopback`: `http://127.0.0.1:7420`, `http://localhost:1`, `http://[::1]:7420` → true; `https://gm.example.com`, `http://10.0.0.5:7420` → false
  - `probeServer` with fake fetch: 200 + `{host:"h"}` → ok; 404 → error; a throw → error; `{host: 1}` → error

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/pages/picker.html`

- Title "graph-manager". Two cards:
  1. **Run on this computer**: "Starts graph-manager here. Your workspaces live in <path>." Fill in the path with `await window.gmDesktop.workspacesDir()`. A button **Run on this computer** calls `gmDesktop.chooseLocal()`.
  2. **Connect to a server**: a URL `<input type="url">` with placeholder `https://graph-manager.example.com`, a **Connect** button, and an error line.
     - On Connect, call `const r = await gmDesktop.checkServer(value)`. If `r.ok === false`, show `r.error`.
     - If `r.insecure`, show "This connection is not encrypted. Your password will be sent in plain text." with **Connect anyway** and **Cancel**.
     - Otherwise, or after Connect anyway, call `gmDesktop.chooseRemote(r.origin)`.
- The Connect button is disabled while a check runs and shows "Checking…".

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/preload.cts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: expose `action(name)` (existing), plus:
  - `workspacesDir()` → `ipcRenderer.invoke("gm:workspacesDir")`
  - `checkServer(url)` → `invoke("gm:checkServer", url)`. It runs `normalizeServerUrl` and then `probeServer` in the main process, and returns `{ ok, origin, insecure }` or `{ ok: false, error }`.
  - `chooseLocal()` → `invoke("gm:chooseLocal")`
  - `chooseRemote(origin)` → `invoke("gm:chooseRemote", origin)`

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/main.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  1. Startup: `const s = readSettings(userData)`.
     - `s.mode === "local"` → local mode, as today.
     - `s.mode === "remote" && s.remoteUrl` → remote mode.
     - Otherwise → the picker window, which loads `dist/pages/picker.html` with the preload.
  2. IPC handlers. Each one checks that `event.senderFrame.url` starts with `file:`.
     - `gm:workspacesDir` returns `localWorkspacesDir(process.env, os.homedir())`.
     - `gm:checkServer` is described above.
     - `gm:chooseLocal` writes `mode: "local"` and starts local mode.
     - `gm:chooseRemote(origin)` runs `normalizeServerUrl(origin)` again and refuses when it isn't `ok`. Then it writes `mode: "remote"` and `remoteUrl`, and starts remote mode.
  3. Remote mode:
     - `probeServer(remoteUrl)`. On failure, show `error.html` with `title="Can't reach <remoteUrl>."`, `detail=<error>` and `actions=retry,change`, or `actions=retry,change,local` when `isLoopback(remoteUrl)`.
     - On success, the main window (`webPreferences: { partition: "persist:remote", contextIsolation: true, sandbox: true, nodeIntegration: false }`, no preload) loads `remoteUrl + "/"`.
     - Use the same link handlers with `appOrigin = remoteUrl`. Child windows use the `persist:remote` partition.
     - `webContents.on("did-fail-load", (e, code, desc, url, isMainFrame) => ...)`: when `isMainFrame` is true and `code !== -3` (aborted), show the same error page (same `actions` rule). This is also what shows when a connected server stops and the user reloads or navigates. In addition, while a loopback remote window is open, poll `probeServer(remoteUrl, fetch, 3000)` every 5 s; on the first failure show the same error page, so a stopped terminal server is noticed without a reload. Stop polling when the window closes or the mode changes.
     - Don't add a `certificate-error` handler. Electron's default refuses bad certificates.
     - The window title is the page title + ` — <host of remoteUrl>`: handle `page-title-updated`, call `event.preventDefault()`, then `win.setTitle(...)`.
  4. `gm:action` gets:
     - `change` → open the picker.
     - `local` (**Run on this computer**) → close the remote window, save `mode: "local"` and start local mode, exactly as the picker's `gm:chooseLocal` does (which may show the "already running" page again if a server came back).
     - `connect` → save `mode: "remote"` with `remoteUrl = "http://127.0.0.1:<N>"` from the already-running page and start this remote mode (replace the minimal window from the earlier task). No plain-`http` warning: it's loopback.
     - Leaving local mode always calls `await server.stop()` before the switch.
     - Switching to remote stops the local server.
     - Switching to local closes the remote window.
  5. Menu: `Menu.setApplicationMenu(Menu.buildFromTemplate(template))`, rebuilt on every mode change.
     - macOS: `{ role: "appMenu" }`, a **File** menu, `{ role: "editMenu" }`, a **View** menu, `{ role: "windowMenu" }` and a **Help** menu. Windows and Linux: the same without `appMenu`; **File** gets `{ role: "quit" }`.
     - **File** items:
       - **Switch to local** (in remote mode) or **Switch to server…** (in local mode); both open the picker
       - **Change server URL…** (remote mode only), which opens the picker with the URL field filled. Pass `?url=<remoteUrl>` and let `picker.html` read it.
       - **Open server log** (local mode only): `shell.openPath(<userData>/logs/server.log)`
       - **Open workspaces folder**: `shell.openPath(workspacesDir)`, after `mkdirSync` with `recursive: true`
     - **View**: `{ role: "reload" }` (Cmd/Ctrl+R) and `{ role: "toggleDevTools" }`.
     - **Help**: **graph-manager on GitHub** → `shell.openExternal("https://github.com/romm0109/graph-execution")`.
  6. Put the template in an exported pure function `menuTemplate(mode, platform, handlers)` in `src/menu.ts`, so its labels can be unit-tested without Electron. Type it as `MenuItemConstructorOptions[]` with `import type` only.
- **GOTCHA**: `import type { MenuItemConstructorOptions } from "electron"` is allowed in `menu.ts`, because type imports are erased. A runtime import of `electron` in any file a test imports is not allowed: vitest would load Electron's npm stub, which only exports a path string.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build -w graph-manager-desktop && npm test -w graph-manager-desktop`

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager-desktop/src/menu.test.ts`

- `menuTemplate("local", "darwin", handlers)`:
  - The first item has `role: "appMenu"`.
  - File contains "Switch to server…" and "Open server log".
  - It doesn't contain "Change server URL…".
- `menuTemplate("remote", "win32", handlers)`:
  - No `appMenu`.
  - File contains "Switch to local", "Change server URL…" and a `quit` role.
  - It doesn't contain "Open server log".
- Calling the File item's `click` calls the matching handler.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With no `desktop.json`, the app opens the picker. **Run on this computer** starts local mode and saves `mode: "local"`.
- [ ] Typing `gm.example.com` checks `https://gm.example.com/api/auth/info`. A failure shows "No graph-manager server answered at https://gm.example.com." and saves nothing.
- [ ] Plain `http://` to a non-local host shows the unencrypted warning with **Connect anyway** and **Cancel**.
- [ ] With `mode: "remote"`, the window shows that server's login page in the `persist:remote` session. After logging in, the login survives an app restart.
- [ ] An unreachable remote server on start shows "Can't reach <url>." with **Retry** and **Change server**; for `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`/`[::1]` also **Run on this computer**, which starts local mode and saves `mode: "local"`.
- [ ] Connected to a graph-manager at `http://127.0.0.1:N` (from **Connect to it**), stopping that server shows the error page with **Run on this computer** within about 5 s.
- [ ] The menu items match the mode. Switching away from local stops the local server.
- [ ] Unit tests for `normalizeServerUrl`, `probeServer` and `menuTemplate` pass. Root checks pass: `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test`.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager && npm run build -w graph-manager-desktop
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager-desktop
```
